NDT software in Dallas: what inspection companies here actually need

If you run an NDT or inspection company in Dallas, the right NDT software is the one that holds your technicians, instruments, jobs, reports and invoices in one system, because the work in this market is spread across very different clients in the same week. The Atlantis ERP solution is built for that mix, and it is configured around how your company already works rather than forcing you into a generic template.

Picture a typical Dallas contractor. On Monday a crew is doing weld inspection on structural steel for a building going up in Uptown or along the Tollway corridor. On Tuesday two Level IIs are on a gas distribution replacement project, and someone else is running mag particle on fabricated parts at a shop in Garland or Grand Prairie. By Thursday you are pricing a power plant outage in the ERCOT market and chasing a bridge subcontract on a TxDOT job. The Dallas economy produces that spread: Energy Transfer and Atmos Energy are headquartered here, Oncor runs transmission and distribution across North Texas, Vistra is based in Irving, Texas Instruments and Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control are local, and DFW Airport and Love Field keep aviation work moving.

The regulators set the paperwork load. Pipeline work answers to PHMSA and the Railroad Commission of Texas, radiography crews work under licences from the Texas Department of State Health Services radiation control program, and aerospace and power clients bring their own auditors. Most Dallas NDT firms are small to mid-sized, often run by a Level III or a former field technician who is tired of chasing spreadsheets. That is the company this page is written for.

ERP for NDT companies in Dallas: the short answer

An ERP for NDT companies in Dallas should connect four things that usually live apart: who is certified to do the work, which instrument is calibrated to do it, where the crew is this week, and what gets billed when the report is signed. The Atlantis NDT ERP does this in one database, with apps for certificates, team assignments, asset management, NDT reports, quotations, invoicing and CRM.

The difference from a general business ERP is that the NDT fields are already there. A technician record carries scheme, level, method, expiry, vision test and OJT hours. An instrument record carries serial number, calibration status and next due date. A job carries site, client PO, methods, codes, acceptance criteria and assigned equipment. A report follows draft, in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures. You do not have to build any of that from scratch.

For a Dallas firm juggling pipeline, structural, power and aerospace clients, that shared record is what stops the classic failures: a technician sent to site with a lapsed MT cert, a UT flaw detector that went out of calibration last week, a report sitting unsigned while the invoice waits. You can see how the apps fit together on the ERP apps overview, or ask for a walkthrough built around your own jobs.

Technician certification tracking software for Dallas crews

Technician certification tracking in the Atlantis ERP records every certificate a technician holds, works out its status automatically, and warns you before anything lapses. Status is computed as active, expiring soon (within 90 days), expired or revoked, and there are dedicated Expiring Soon and Expired menus so nobody has to hunt.

Each certificate stores the scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), level from trainee through Level III, method, certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, industry sector, OJT and training hours, exam results and attachments. That matters in Dallas because your people often carry more than one scheme. A technician who works pipeline RT for a midstream client under your SNT-TC-1A written practice may also hold an aerospace qualification recorded under other for a Lockheed Martin supplier, and a CWI or client-specific card on top.

Vision tests are tracked separately with near vision (Jaeger J1/J2), far vision, colour perception, contrast, examiner, clinic and expiry. Daily checks create warning tasks 90 days before a cert or vision test runs out, and configurable email alerts go to whoever you choose, with your own look-ahead days and resend interval. The employee NDT profile also holds radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry, which is what a radiation safety officer wants to see before a crew heads to a pipeline tie-in. Timesheets warn when a technician's certificate is not valid, so a lapse gets caught at the point of billing too. Details are on the certificates app page.

Crew dispatch and scheduling software across the Metroplex

Crew dispatch in the Atlantis ERP runs jobs as team assignments that move from planned to dispatched to in field to submitted to closed. Each assignment carries site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates, so the office knows who is where across a metro area that stretches from Denton to Waxahachie.

The technician availability calendar holds assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable days, and overlaps are blocked. Double-booking a technician is blocked, and so is double-booking an equipment serial number. That second point bites Dallas firms hard: the same phased array unit gets promised to a fabrication shop in Grand Prairie and to a refinery-style piping job out of town because two coordinators each thought it was free. In the ERP, the second booking simply will not save.

When a coordinator assigns an instrument that is out of calibration, the system warns them at the moment of assignment, not after the report has gone to the client. Each technician shows current assignment, utilisation, and next available date, which is what you need when a utility client calls at 4pm asking for two MT Level IIs tomorrow morning. You can work in calendar, kanban or list view depending on who is looking. Time Off requests feed the same availability calendar, so approved leave is visible to dispatch without a second spreadsheet. More on the team assignments app.

Calibration management software for Dallas instrument fleets

Calibration management in the Atlantis ERP tracks every flaw detector, probe, yoke, densitometer and other instrument by serial number, with calibration frequency, status and next due date. Calibration certificates sit in a register with the lab's accreditation number, valid, expiring or expired status, the PDF itself and expiry alerts.

Each calibration record captures the provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, whether the lab is accredited, and a pass, fail or conditional result. Instruments move through a lifecycle of new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired and disposed, so you can see at a glance that three UT sets are away at the lab this week. The issue and return workflow records condition at checkout and check-in with supervisor and manager approval, and reservations prevent clashes.

The maintenance log covers preventive, corrective, repair, cleaning, firmware update and probe replacement work with condition before and after. Consumables such as couplant, penetrant, developer, magnetic particles and PPE carry reorder levels and a low-stock flag, which helps when the MT bench in your Dallas yard is supporting several shop jobs at once. Purchase records mark vendors as OEM, dealer or calibration lab, with the accredited-lab flag and accreditation expiry, and order lines can be tied to a specific equipment serial. When an aerospace or power client's auditor asks for the calibration trail of the UT set used on a given day, it is one lookup. See the asset management app.

NDT reporting software for Dallas structural, pipeline and power work

The NDT reports app produces method-specific reports for 17 report types, including UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, PAUT, TOFD, MFL, UT thickness, hardness, PMI, ferrite, holiday/coating and computed radiography. Each type has its own numbering sequence, and every report runs through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent.

For Dallas work that means the structural UT on a moment connection captures the probe calibration table, the pipeline RT on a gas main captures source, technique, IQI type and placement, and the shop MT captures technique and particle type. Weld and job lines carry defect type and orientation, and the overall result is recorded as acceptable, not acceptable or acceptable with remarks. References to work order, request, WPS, contract, drawing numbers, procedure and standard are captured on the report, which is what a general contractor's QA manager or a utility's inspection lead wants to see.

Reports can be produced from your own versioned templates in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML with your logo, header and footer, and Excel templates fill automatically by mapping fields to cells. Technicians on a jobsite without signal use the offline field app: pick the method, capture photos, sign on screen, preview the PDF, and it syncs when the truck gets back into coverage. Third-party or authorized inspector names and signatures can be added where the client requires them. For clients who want to see results on a 3D model of the structure or plant, the Digital Twin Reporting Software and Atlantis Digital Twins sit alongside the ERP.

Procedures and written practice control

The procedures app keeps a register of every NDT procedure with document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard such as ASME Section V, acceptance criteria and the body text or uploaded file. Procedures move from draft to submitted, reviewed, approved and published, and approved revisions are locked.

Dallas contractors often write client-specific procedures: one for a midstream operator's pipeline RT, another for an aerospace supplier's penetrant line, another for structural UT to AWS D1.1 on a building project. Keeping those straight across revisions is exactly where audits go wrong. The ERP keeps full revision history with a snapshot of each revision, records who prepared, reviewed and approved it and when, and captures a reason when a draft is rejected. Approvers get email notifications and reminders for anything waiting on them.

There is also an AI-assisted first draft for a new procedure, falling back to a built-in template, which saves your Level III from starting at a blank page. The Level III still reviews, edits and approves it; the tool drafts, it does not sign. Procedure and WPS references then flow into project tasks and reports, so the report on the Grand Prairie shop job points at the revision that was actually in force.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Dallas contractors

Quoting and invoicing in the Atlantis ERP are tied to the same job, so the quote, the timesheets and the invoice all describe the same work. Quotes carry job type, site, project dates and applicable codes, with NDT service products flagged by method and category and a branded quotation PDF.

Clients can accept and sign quotes online, and an accepted quote converts to a sales order without retyping. Invoices carry the NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector, with subtotals for labour, equipment and consumables. Invoice lines can show cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type and days or hours, which is the level of detail a Dallas general contractor or utility usually asks for before approving payment.

Timesheets record work type (inspection, travel, standby, setup), method, billable flag, rate multiplier, site, client and equipment serial, with approval. Standby on a construction site waiting for the steel erector is a real cost in this market, and when it is recorded properly it gets billed. Field expenses and per diems for out-of-town crews go through the Expenses app and can be re-billed to the job. The financial dashboard shows revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA, outstanding invoices and a 12-month view. See the quotations and invoicing apps.

Winning work in DFW: CRM built for NDT sales

The CRM app records the fields that matter when you sell inspection services: service line, lead source, NDT service type, industry sector, site country, and estimated technicians and days. Each lead gets an NDT lead score from 0 to 100, grouped as hot, warm, nurture or cold.

In Dallas the pipeline of opportunities is wide: general contractors on commercial towers, fabrication shops across Tarrant and Dallas counties, utilities, midstream companies, data center builders along the I-35 and I-20 corridors, and aviation maintenance. You can import leads from CSV, preview AI-personalised emails, and enrol a lead in a drip email sequence by service line, with pause, resume and unsubscribe handled. The AI Marketing app writes newsletter, promotion, nurture and announcement emails using an AI model that can run on your own server.

The Business Cards app is useful after a local trade event or a pre-bid meeting: photograph a card and the name, company, title, email, phones and website are extracted, then one click creates a CRM lead or adds the contact to a mailing list. Enquiry forms on your company website feed straight into the CRM, so a request from a Plano fabricator does not sit in a shared inbox.

Inspection management software in Dallas: dashboards and integrations

Inspection management software earns its keep when the owner can see the whole business on one screen. The Atlantis ERP includes KPI dashboards showing calibration due and overdue, certificates expiring and expired, and issued equipment that is overdue for return, next to the financial dashboard.

Many Dallas firms already use an accounting package or have a client that runs a large maintenance system. The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections, scoped during implementation. A common pattern is keeping QuickBooks for the accountant while the ERP runs operations, or pushing approved report data to a utility client's system. The field-device API also handles jobs assigned to a technician, equipment issued to them, report submission and sync.

Fleet records matter too: vehicle purpose, whether the vehicle can carry radioactive sources, transport licence number and expiry, and assignment to a project and driver with dates and mileage. For an RT crew running between a Dallas yard and pipeline spreads outside the Metroplex, that is part of a clean audit trail.

Affordable, customizable ERP for inspection companies in Dallas: implementation

The Atlantis ERP is affordable, accessible and fully customizable, and pricing is quote on request because it depends on which apps you need and how much configuration your company requires. Implementation is done by Atlantis NDT, founded by an ASNT NDT Level III, so the people setting it up understand written practices, calibration intervals and client report formats.

A typical Dallas rollout starts with a working session on your current jobs: which clients, which methods, which report formats, which schemes your technicians hold. Technicians, certificates and vision tests are loaded first, then instruments with calibration history, then procedures. Report templates are set up to match what your clients already accept, including Excel templates mapped cell by cell. Taxes, payment terms and invoice layout are configured for Texas during implementation, and integrations are scoped at the same time.

Training for office staff and field technicians follows, with the offline field app installed on the devices your crews already carry. If you also train technicians, the eLearning app provides a course portal with Level I, II and III sections, protected video lessons, quizzes and completion certificates, alongside the Practical NDT 3D simulator. Atlantis offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A based NDT training. To see this on your own data, book a Dallas ERP demo.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT software for a Dallas inspection company?

The best NDT software is one that links certificates, calibration, dispatch, reports and invoicing in one system. The Atlantis ERP does this for Dallas contractors working across pipeline, structural, power, fabrication and aerospace clients, and it is configured to your written practice and report formats.

Is the Atlantis ERP suitable for small NDT companies in Dallas?

Yes. Small firms use the same apps and start with the ones they need most, usually certificates, asset management, team assignments and NDT reports. It is affordable and quoted on request, so a five-person shop is not paying for a setup built for a large contractor.

Does it work on jobsites without signal?

Yes. The offline field app stores drafts and photos on the device and syncs later, with method picker, photo capture, on-screen signature and PDF preview.

Can it track aerospace qualifications as well as SNT-TC-1A?

Yes. Certificates can be recorded under SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other, so client-specific and aerospace qualifications sit next to your written-practice certifications with their own expiry dates.

Can it connect to QuickBooks or a client's SAP or Maximo?

Yes. The ERP has an open REST API and integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections. The scope is agreed during implementation.

How long does implementation take in Dallas?

It depends on how many apps you start with and how much data you bring. Most of the effort is loading technicians, instruments and report templates. We give you a plan after the first working session. Request an implementation plan.
